evidence: frontend/apps/reality-web/src/app/[locale]/profile/page.tsx:17,65 — the authenticated /[locale]/profile page renders entirely fabricated data: `const profile = MOCK_PROFILE` and it maps MOCK_LISTINGS / MOCK_ACTIVITY / MOCK_REVIEWS. It is wrapped in ProtectedRoute (SSO), so every LOGGED-IN user — regardless of identity — is shown the same hardcoded persona 'Tomáš Novotný' with fake PII (email t.novotny@email.sk, phone +421 911 123 456 in _mock.ts:46-57), fake stats (12 active listings, 47 deals, 4.7★), and 3 fabricated listings/activity/reviews.

frontend/apps/reality-web/src/app/[locale]/profile/_mock.ts — the mock is the sole data source; there is no live-data path. The page comment itself concedes it is a stub: 'Once /users/me + /listings/by-owner endpoints land, replace MOCK_* with live data via the SDK' — i.e. a known placeholder shipped on a real authenticated route, not a dev-only fixture.

Impact: a real user reaching their own profile sees someone else's fabricated identity/PII presented as their account — a completeness gap that reads as a privacy/trust bug on a public portal. Contrast PopularNeighbourhoods.tsx, whose hardcoded set is documented as an intentional curated marketing surface; this profile mock is not intentional, it is unfinished.

Landable frontend-only fix: gate the page on real /users/me + listings-by-owner SDK calls (with loading/empty/error states), or hide the tabbed profile behind a 'coming soon' state, until the endpoints land — do not render fabricated PII to authenticated users.

frontend/apps/reality-web/src/components/comparison/ComparisonUrlHandler.tsx:43-47 — the shared-comparison loader fetches each id from `${getApiBase()}/api/v1/listings/${id}` and does `return response.json() as Promise<ListingSummary>` with NO runtime shape validation, then pushes result.value straight into addToComparison → rendered by ComparisonView (used on /[locale]/compare/page.tsx).

This diverges from the repo's own established hardening for the SAME endpoint family: src/app/[locale]/listings/[slug]/page.tsx:88-89 routes every 200 body through parseListingDetail() precisely because (its comment) 'A 200 does not guarantee a well-formed body … Rendering such a body crashes SSR'. The comparison path has no equivalent normalizer.

ComparisonView.tsx derefs listing fields per-row (row.getValue(l) across listings.map at lines 271/301); a malformed-but-truthy 200 (proxy partial response, wrong-typed collection field) for a shared id can therefore surface a broken/crashing comparison client-side instead of being dropped.

Landable frontend-only fix: validate/normalize each fetched body (reuse a ListingSummary parser mirroring parseListingDetail) before addToComparison; drop ids whose body fails the shape check, consistent with the existing per-id Promise.allSettled graceful-degrade.

frontend/apps/reality-web/src/lib/comparison-context.tsx:37-46 — on mount the provider does `const parsed = JSON.parse(stored); setListings(parsed)` with no Array.isArray/shape guard. The try/catch only defends against JSON syntax errors, not a syntactically-valid-but-wrong-typed value (e.g. `"null"`, `"{}"`, `"42"`).

A non-array `parsed` then flows into listings and every consumer assumes an array: the save effect (line 55) reads `listings.length`, isInComparison (line 66) calls `.some`, removeFromComparison `.filter`, ComparisonView `.map` — all throw on a non-array, and ComparisonProvider wraps a large part of the app, so a single corrupted `ppt-comparison` localStorage entry (user/extension-editable) hard-crashes the surrounding tree with no recovery (the catch that would clear it is only around JSON.parse).

Landable frontend-only fix: after JSON.parse, guard `if (!Array.isArray(parsed)) { localStorage.removeItem(STORAGE_KEY); return; }` (and ideally filter to items with a string id) before setListings — mirrors the defensive-parse pattern already used in lib/auth-token.ts getSession().
